title: How Long Is Splatoon Raiders
description: The Splatoon franchise has historically focused on chaotic multiplayer mayhem that pits teams against each other to see who can emerge from the paint victorious. While the games have featured campaigns, these supplementary modes have largely felt more like training grounds than fully fleshed-out experiences. That all changes with Splatoon Raiders. Splatoon Raiders is the series' first foray into a strictly campaign-focused adventure, unleashing players onto a mysterious set of islands to search for treasure and find a way home. And since this game lacks the competitive multiplayer modes that have defined the franchise so far, that means you'll be tackling objectives at your own pace, either alone or in online co-op. If you want to know just how long it might take you to do so, let's take a look. How long is Splatoon Raiders? An average playthrough of Splatoon Raiders will take around 15-18 hours. This includes playing through the game's main missions while engaging moderately in its optional content, such as completing tasks that reward additional outfits, tinkering with dozens of weapon variations, and searching for some hidden Salmonid Relic collectibles. Of course, the time spent beating the game will also vary based on which of the three difficulty choices you pick: Tourist (Easy), Raider (Medium), or Survivalist (Hard). Fully completing the game is far more challenging, of course, and can take considerably longer to accomplish. Collecting every weapon, gadget, outfit, and Salmonid Relic can add significant playtime to your save file. After beating the campaign, you can dive back in alone or with friends to tackle a difficult endgame that demands you consistently upgrade your gear and prepare well for each raid. If you're aiming to complete Splatoon Raiders' post-game campaign, you can easily push past the 40-hour mark --but the fun doesn't stop there, either. Much of the appeal of this game is playing with friends (and strangers), meaning there's a lot of fun…

title: How To Get Halo: Campaign Evolved Early Access
description: With the Halo: Campaign Evolved release date looming, it's not too late to get early access to play the reboot of the first game in the Halo franchise before most other people. While Campaign Evolved will be on Game Pass from day one, there are a few extra steps you'll need to secure early access. You'll need to preorder Premium Edition of the game to get up to five days early access. As an extra bonus, you'll also receive the Foundry Armoury Pack which has five Master Chief armor skins and six weapon skins. There's also a digital artbook and short story, as well as the game manual. The Premium Edition costs $69.99, but if you've already preordered the standard version and want to upgrade, that'll set you back $20. You can find both versions on the Xbox, PlayStation, or Steam storefronts. While the standard version of the game releases on July 28, Halo: Campaign Evolved early access begins on July 23. However, you don't have to preorder the game before that date to get in. You can preorder at any point before July 28 to get immediate access. title: Is Halo: Campaign Evolved Steam Deck Verified?
description: The Halo: Campaign Evolved release date is right around the corner, and it's coming even sooner for those that have early access. Campaign Evolved takes players back to the first game in the series, adding new missions and overhauling the graphics. In a teaser posted to the official Halo X account, there's clear footage of the game being played on a Steam Deck. Alongside the messaging that clarifies that Halo: Campaign Evolved will offer cross-platform four-player co-op, this is an indication that Halo: Campaign Evolved is playable on Steam Deck. Alongside this, in a Q&A posted to Halo Waypoint, the official website for the franchise, it's stated that Halo: Campaign Evolved is Steam Deck Verified. It's also optimized for Windows handhelds, so if your portable gaming device of choice is something like the ROG Ally instead, you'll still be able to enjoy it to its full potential. For those on less portable devices, Halo: Campaign Evolved will be on Game Pass from day one for certain subscription tiers. Halo Games, Ranked – The Best Halo FPS Games View Images

title: Maybe Not Everything Needs To Be A Fortnite Collab
description: Honestly, I thought I could no longer be surprised by the off-the-wall collaborations between Fortnite and various other IPs. At this point in Fortnite's very lucrative lifespan, the general rule of thumb seems to be, "If it's popular, it's gonna end up in Fortnite." Damn near every Marvel Cinematic Universe character has made an appearance, countless musical artists have held in-game concerts, and Epic has always been very good at making sure that whatever the internet is obsessed with at any given moment ends up tied to the game in one way or another. The problem is that the internet is currently obsessed with Curry Barker's wildly successful horror film, Obsession. Epic Games and Blumhouse Productions apparently thought this would be a good time to release a collaborative ad for both Fortnite and Barker's film, which just hit streaming services after an extended theatrical run. The one-minute ad features various "jump-scare" moments from Obsession, but replaces the film's female lead, Nikki (Inde Navarrette), with a Galaxy Zero Point Sprite (the rarest collectible Sprite in Fortnite, with a drop rate of roughly 1 in 300 million). Instead of using a One Wish Willow as he did in the film, main character Bear (Michael Johnston) is shown snapping a "One Llama Luck" stick in half, causing the Sprite to become obsessed with him. Editor's note: The following includes major spoilers for Obsession, and also contains references to sexual assault. If you haven't seen the film, the video reads as a silly little nod to how obsessed Fortnite players are with the extremely rare Sprite. If you have seen the film, this entire ad spot is baffling at best and offensive at worst. In Obsession, Nikki loses her autonomy after Bear wishes that Nikki "loved [him] more than anyone in the f***ing world." Bear gets his wish, but it quickly becomes apparent that the real Nikki is trapped inside her body, unable to control it as she has been possessed by whatever magic lies within the One…

title: This Horror Game Is Getting Mixed Reviews, But Its Best Parts Are Amazing
description: Of all the games Lethal Company has inspired over these last few years, none of them have taken the concept in such an interesting new direction as The Mound: Omen of Cthulhu. While the game definitely lacks polish, as a horror-obsessive person, I feel comfy saying that fans of horror or horror-extraction games haven't played something quite like The Mound before, and that's mainly owed to its brilliant core mechanic: tripping balls. I covered a preview build of The Mound a few weeks ago, but if you missed it, it's a four-player co-op horror game set in the age of exploration with a Lethal Company-like twist. With your pals in tow, you'll embark on a quest into Lovecraftian wilderness to extract enough loot to meet your quota from the trading company back home. It sounds familiar--this setup is the gameplay loop dujour in the horror world, and has been for some years now. But it's easier said than done when the world is constantly messing with your head. You'll see things that aren't there. You won't see things that are there. You'll even sometimes see your friends as monsters, and need to do your best to see through the illusion before you hack them to bits. The Mound explains very little to you from the outset, and that's its secret weapon. You'll come to discover how things work over time, but even then, knowing is half the battle. You'll know to dodge zombie-like monsters because they can pounce on you from range. You'll definitely do a 180 and sprint away from the massive, spider-like creatures that explode on you when they get close enough. It's so creepy how nearly silent they are, too. It's made me unsure of when it's safe to turn around again. There are strange birds in some trees that, if you don't pick them off quickly and cleanly, seem to disrupt your surroundings even more. The "rules" of the world feel elusive. The Mound is a game of hallucinations, of not trusting what you're seeing or hearing. I've put in several hours with this slow-burn nightmare,…

title: Darkest Dungeon Is Getting New DLC, Even Though It Has A Sequel
description: Red Hook Studios surprised Darkest Dungeon fans by announcing new DLC for the first game years after a sequel was already released. It's titled The Fire's Edge and will be out in August. Darkest Dungeon exited early access in 2016 and last received DLC in May 2020. In the six years since, Red Hook launched a sequel that builds on the strong foundations of the first game and has supported it with DLC. That's why it's a bit surprising to see the developers return to the game that started it all. The decision makes a little more sense when you learn that The Fire's Edge will bring some Darkest Dungeon 2 concepts into its predecessor. Namely, The Duelist and The Runaway heroes from the sequel will make their way back to the original. The Duelist benefits from moving around the party and switching between aggressive and defensive stances, while The Runaway will have access to the unique Burn damage type. Darkest Dungeon: The Fire's Edge To mix up Darkest Dungeon's roguelike runs even more once these new characters arrive, The Fire's Edge is adding new mechanics to equippable trinkets and the Academie Duello, Craftworks, and Archaeological Base Camp Hamlet districts to explore. If you've only been playing the sequel in recent years, this DLC looks like it'll give you a good reason to come back. The developers have confirmed that The Fire's Edge will be paid DLC, although we have not learned how much it will retail for yet. Red Hook also explained that it is trying to make sure this DLC won't break existing mods and that an "improved mod manager" for the original Darkest Dungeon is in the works. Darkest Dungeon: The Fire's Edge will be released on PC, PS4, and Nintendo Switch on August 18. If you're worried about the fact that Darkest Dungeon 2 isn't getting any love from Red Hook right now, the series' X account confirmed that DLC for the sequel will follow in 2027.

Ubisoft Reacts To Ghost Recon Leaks, Promises News In August
description: Ubisoft has confirmed that it will share what's next for Ghost Recon when it celebrates the series' 25th anniversary on August 6. This comes after several reports and rumors about upcoming Ghost Recon games emerged over the past month. On July 20, Insider Gaming reported on a leak of the Ghost Recon: Wildlands Definitive Edition, a current-generation remaster of the 2017 game that will add a new mission, support 4K resolution, and run at 60 frames per second. It claimed that this is part of an "upgrade treatment" initiative within Ubisoft, and meant to tide players over until the next mainline Ghost Recon comes out. Insider Gaming had previously reported that the newest Ghost Recon, codenamed Project OVR, cut features like helicopters and proximity mines after failing an alpha test earlier this spring. Ubisoft finally felt that these leaks and rumors were worth addressing, so it put out a brief message on the franchise's official X account, which has rarely posted over the last couple of years, to confirm when fans will learn more. The latest game in this Tom Clancy-inspired franchise is 2019's Ghost Recon: Breakpoint. A battle royale titled Ghost Recon: Frontline was announced by Ubisoft in 2021, but it was canceled less than a year later. As it has been nearly seven years since the series' last new game, it's understandable why Ghost Recon fans are itching to learn more. Following Ubisoft's Creative House restructuring earlier this year amid layoffs, the Ghost Recon project fell under the purview of Creative House 2. Christoph Hartmann, who founded 2K Games and was VP of Amazon Game Studios, took over as Creative House 2's general manager earlier this month. Whatever Ubisoft announces on August 6 will be some of the first Creative House 2 titles under Hartmann's stewardship.

title: Warner Bros. Acquisition Is Stuck In Legal Limbo Again
description: Paramount Skydance's plan to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery has hit yet another snag, as a judge has issued a two-week pause on its planned acquisition. After a coalition of 12 state attorneys --led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta--argued that the merger would violate federal antitrust law and potentially lead to higher film and TV prices, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin placed a temporary pause on the merger. The order could be extended from 14 to 28 days, and Paramount Skydance was originally expecting to close the deal on July 22 (via Variety ). "Plaintiff States' showing at least demonstrates that serious questions going to the merits remain, weighing in favor of preliminary injunctive relief," Martinez-Olguin said. "Paramount and Warner Bros. will continue to operate as separate, viable companies competing in the marketplace while they wait for the Court to adjudicate this case." Bonta labeled the ruling as a "critical first win" in the coalition's case (via NBC News ), while Paramount Skydance has continued to insist that the lawsuit represents a "fundamentally flawed application" of antitrust laws. "With our lawsuit, we're fighting for a free and fair market and a thriving film and television industry that serves creatives and audiences alike. We have a full tank of gas, the law on our side, and look forward to continuing to make our case," Bonta said. Paramount Skydance claims that acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery will allow it to better compete with the likes of Disney and Netflix, and in addition to all the film IP, studios, sports properties, and television networks it'll gain if the deal passes, it'll also take control of Warner Bros. Games. This would mean that Paramount Skydance would become the new owner of valuable video game IP like Hogwarts Legacy and Mortal Kombat, which could join its new in-house game development studio, Paramount Games Studio. The new arm of Paramount Skydance already has several projects in development, including a…

title: Nintendo Basically Says That Splatoon 4 Will Happen
description: While Splatoon Raiders looks like a pivot from Nintendo's competitive multiplayer-focused franchise, a producer on the series confirmed that PvP gameplay in Splatoon will endure, even uttering the phrase "Splatoon 4" in an interview. Nintendo's Ask the Developer feature (per Nintendo Life ) included a question that straight-up asked producer Seita Inoue why a spin-off is the franchise's next entry instead of a proper Splatoon 4. Inoue clarified that though Raiders is a markedly different game, Nintendo will "continue to develop competitive gameplay going forward." In short, the reasons for creating Raiders "as a spin-off and not as 'Splatoon 4'" came from Nintendo's desire to create "something with a slightly different approach to gameplay" and "a new entry point into the series," according to Inoue. Citing the PvE Salmon Run mode from Splatoon 2 and 3 and the single-player story modes in all three mainline games, Inoue emphasized that the series "isn’t just about competitive play." In Inoue's words, Nintendo has been "going full speed ahead for over 11 years since the series’ launch, developing and updating three titles along the way." Splatoon 3 was a sales hit when it launched in 2022, so making a fourth, traditional Splatoon game as a Switch 2 exclusive is an easy prediction to make. These comments from Splatoon developers only solidify the possibility further. GameSpot's Splatoon Raiders review calls it "loads of fun," with "a single-player campaign that’s much more satisfying than its past attempts to inject a story campaign into the main games." The Switch 2 game releases on July 23. Nintendo’s Top-Selling Switch 2 Games Of All Time View Images

title: Hasbro Is Betting On Fewer, Bigger Video Games After $56 Million Write-Down
description: Hasbro's ambitious plan to expand into video games appears to have hit an expensive snag, as the company has recorded a $56 million impairment charge related to its video games portfolio for 2028 and beyond, according to its second-quarter earnings results. For the uninitiated, an impairment charge is a sudden loss of value for an asset, making it worth far less than what a company originally paid for it. "Over the last several quarters, we have reviewed our portfolio and updated our plans for Hasbro's digital future," Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks said to shareholders. "That work included canceling several games scheduled for release in 2028 and beyond and recording a $56 million non-cash write-down this quarter for related capitalized costs. The write-down reflects the standard we are applying to the portfolio. We are focusing our digital investment behind the franchises, platforms, and partners where we see the clearest upside and where Hasbro has the strongest right to win." According to Cocks, Hasbro will have four priorities going forward for its video game projects--focus, cost discipline, ownable platforms, and partnership. The plan includes a new focus on "trading card games and role-playing games," a decrease in total digital spend, prioritizing its own IP, and finding the right partners for these projects. Cocks cited Scopely as a prime example, as the studio's work on Monopoly Go is expected to exceed a lifetime revenue of $8 billion later this year. While Hasbro had big video game plans lined up, recent years have seen the company scale back and cancel several of its projects. It hasn't detailed exactly which games got cut, but it did mention that sci-fi adventure Exodus and its Dungeons & Dragons game Warlock are still scheduled to launch in 2027. While Atomic Arcade--the studio behind a new GI Joe game featuring fan-favorite character Snake Eyes--had layoffs earlier this year, Hasbro said that the developer's project still remains in development. title: We Finally Know Xal’atath’s Evil Plan For The World Of Warcraft
description: After years of theories and speculation, World of Warcraft players may have finally uncovered the real endgame of its current main villain, Xal'atath. Xal'atath has been Azeroth's big bad for the past several expansions, but aside from amassing power in her Dark Heart artifact, her exact motivations haven't been entirely clear. She doesn't seem to work for the Old Gods but for herself, though to what end has been up for debate. Now, a datamined bit of dialogue from the game's upcoming 12.1 update may have just revealed her ultimate goal: one that will almost certainly spell doom for Azeroth and perhaps even the entire Warcraft universe. Potential spoilers for patch 12.1 and future updates below. As spotted by Reddit user rapunzel1213, a datamined (and likely subject-to-change) script from the game's 12.1 public-test realm looks to have revealed Xal'atath's true goal, and it's not to corrupt or destroy Azeroth. No, it's to become Azeroth herself. For a little context, the last few expansions have built up the idea that within the planet Azeroth is a slumbering Worldsoul, essentially an unborn cosmic entity called a Titan. Azeroth, however, is not just any Worldsoul, but the Prime Worldsoul. It's for that reason Azeroth seems to be in many ways the center of the Warcraft universe. The Titans sought to protect Azeroth's Worldsoul, the Burning Legion sought to destroy it, and the Void aimed to corrupt it, knowing it would be the most powerful being in the universe were it to ever awaken. Xal'atath, it seems, is looking to become the ultimate power in the universe by somehow merging with Azeroth's Worldsoul. The datamined script looks to be part of patch 12.1's Epilogue, setting up the events of patch 12.2. In it, Arator and Orweyna arrive to deliver an urgent message to Blood Elf leaders Lor'themar and Liadrin. "Xal'atath has reached the Worldsoul," Arator says. "We have to move now. We have to find a way down there, blast open the coreway, anything." Liadrin asks if…
